title: Quick check: Legacy Class Component Maintenance

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Legacy Class Component Maintenance”?
options: Existing lifecycle methods should use state setters and immutable next values so React can update the UI predictably.
The concept removes the need to consider error states or accessibility.
The browser will infer all application behavior even if inputs and state are contradictory.
The concept allows application code to mutate React-managed DOM and state directly.
questions.answer_key: Existing lifecycle methods should use state setters and immutable next values so React can update the UI predictably.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Legacy Class Component Maintenance: Existing lifecycle methods should use state setters and immutable next values so React can update the UI predictably.

questions.prompt: Which practice is most reliable when applying Existing lifecycle methods?
options: Skip validation because a successful render proves that the application is correct.
Store duplicate copies of every value so each component can change it independently.
Optimize by adding every available Hook without measuring the result.
Use functional updates when the new value depends on previous state, and do not mutate objects or arrays.
questions.answer_key: Use functional updates when the new value depends on previous state, and do not mutate objects or arrays.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Legacy Class Component Maintenance: Use functional updates when the new value depends on previous state, and do not mutate objects or arrays.

questions.answer_key: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
